exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Hip pain after delivery in mothers
Problems with daily activities in mothers
Lower hours of sleeping in children
cohort: 600 mother-child dyads in Bangladesh, with 300 mothers having undergone cesarean section and 300 having undergone vaginal delivery in their most recent live births.
finding: Mothers who had a cesarean section were more likely to experience health problems such as headache, hip pain, and problems with daily activities, while their children were more likely to have breathing problems, frequent illnesses, lower food demand, and lower sleep duration.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a higher likelihood of health problems in both mothers and their children.
